jobs.title: AI Engineer: Agents & Evaluation
jobs.description: Duties & Accountabilities • Agent engineering: design and build the initial BA, Dev, and QA agents: prompt architecture, context assembly, tool use, and schema-validated JSON outputs, with prompts and skills packs versioned in git and treated as core IP. • Retrieval & context: build the codebase retrieval layer (syntax-aware chunking with tree-sitter, embeddings in pgvector) and the context-pack system: project glossary, org conventions, constraint register, and exemplar retrieval. • Evaluation harness: own the golden dataset (2530 expert-verified items) and the harness that runs nightly in CI: per-agent scores against published acceptance bars, trend monitoring, and regression alerts that block release. • Failure modes: design for the ways agents fail: schema-repair loops, reject-loop re-invocation with reviewer comments injected, retrieval-verified symbols to guard against hallucinated APIs, and honest gap declaration over coverage inflation. • Confidence & quality: implement and tune the confidence-scoring model that routes low-confidence outputs to senior review, and use every human modification (deltas captured at the gates) as improvement signal. • Token economics: own cost per story: per-invocation token and cost telemetry, model-mix tuning (fast tier for enrichment and test generation, top tier for code), and budget-aware prompt design. • AI-native practice: work daily with agentic coding tools; the friction you hit is product input. Education & Experience • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including 2.5+ years building LLM-powered applications in real production use, not prototypes or side projects. • Demonstrable experience with retrieval-augmented generation and context engineering in a production system. • Experience building or operating systematic evaluation for LLM outputs (golden datasets, regression harnesses, rubric scoring). • Experience in a startup or small-team environment is a strong plus. • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrable experience. Technical Skills Required • Strong Python and production experience with LLM provider APIs (Anthropic Claude family experience valued); structured outputs and JSON-schema validation. • Prompt and context engineering with measurable iteration, exemplar selection, context budgeting, instruction design for consistency. • Embeddings and vector search in production (pgvector or similar); code-aware chunking and indexing is a strong plus. • Evaluation engineering: building harnesses, defining acceptance bars, wiring them into CI, and reading the trends. • Token and cost optimisation: metering, model-tier routing, and cost-per-outcome thinking. • Agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph or similar) are a strong plus, as is SQL fluency for telemetry analysis. • Practical, hands-on fluency with modern agentic coding tools (e.g., Claude Code or equivalent) is required. 5-9 Yrs Artificial Intelligence, Engineering, Generation, Python, Vector, DBMS, Evaluation

Proofs of Concept (PoCs), prototypes, hackathons, and experimental trials will not qualify toward the mandatory 3 years of production GenAI experience. A. GenAI Solution Architecture & Engineering Design end-to-end enterprise GenAI application architectures covering UI, API gateways, orchestration, model inference, retrieval, enterprise data integration, observability, security, and infrastructure. Integrate AI agents with enterprise APIs, databases, business applications, and automation platforms. Implement guardrails, human-in-the-loop approval gates, tool authorization, and escalation mechanisms. Apply bounded autonomy, execution limits, timeout handling, idempotency, retries, and compensating transactions. Maintain auditable decision traces, tool execution records, and explanations for consequential agent actions. Evaluate the suitability of deterministic workflows versus agent-based architectures based on business risks and requirements. D. Production Engineering, LLMOps & Scalability Develop scalable backend services using Python, FastAPI, REST APIs, and asynchronous programming. Package and deploy applications using Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud-native infrastructure. Establish production-grade LLMOps practices covering model configuration, prompt versioning, evaluation gates, deployment, monitoring, and rollback. Implement observability across application traces, model calls, retrieval operations, agent execution, and infrastructure. Optimize p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token consumption, inference cost, and infrastructure utilization. Implement load testing, performance benchmarking, failure recovery, and production incident management. Support cloud, hybrid, and on-premises deployment environments. Define service-level objectives (SLOs), operational runbooks, and production support processes. E. AI Quality, Evaluation & Responsible AI Develop automated evaluation pipelines for retrieval performance, answer faithfulness, relevance, completeness, and task success. Build representative golden datasets and regression test suites. Implement human evaluation and LLM-as-judge methodologies with appropriate calibration and validation. Evaluate agents for tool-selection correctness, workflow completion, policy compliance, and unsafe actions. Apply enterprise IAM, RBAC/ABAC, encryption, secrets management, audit logging, and data retention requirements. Work within applicable AI governance and security standards, including relevant practices from ISO/IEC 42001 and OWASP guidance for LLM applications. F. Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) & Stakeholder Engagement A critical requirement of this role is the ability to operate as a Forward Deployed Engineer, combining technical depth with direct business engagement and accountable delivery. Work directly with customers and business stakeholders to understand operational challenges and translate them into viable AI solution architectures. Lead technical discovery, requirements engineering, feasibility assessment, solution design, implementation, and production deployment. Independently investigate complex enterprise environments, legacy applications, data constraints, and integration challenges. Develop reusable architectural patterns, accelerators, deployment templates, and AI engineering assets. Conduct architecture reviews and explain design decisions to engineering teams, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders. Drive adoption, knowledge transfer, user enablement, and operational handover. jobs.title: Artificial Intelligence Engineer
jobs.description: Why this role exists Our existing AI work needs a single accountable engineer for design, monitoring, cost and quality. Every AI feature touches protected health information (PHI) and some influence clinical or financial decisions, so engineering discipline and compliance are not optional. We want someone who knows Claude deeply and also understands the wider AI landscape well enough to choose the right tool, including when that tool is not an LLM. What you will do Build Design and ship Claude-powered features: ambient or dictated visit-note drafting, chart summarization, patient message triage and reply drafts, prior-authorization and appeal letters, referral summaries. Build revenue cycle automation: charge and code suggestions (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS, modifiers), claim scrubbing, denial analysis and appeal drafting, eligibility and remittance (835) reconciliation, A/R follow-up prioritization. Build agentic workflows with tool use and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that read from and write to the EHR and billing database through narrow, audited, least-privilege interfaces. Build retrieval (RAG) over clinical guidelines, payer policies, fee schedules and internal SOPs, with citations back to the source. Integrate with the EHR, practice management, clearinghouse (Waystar) and patient portal through FHIR R4, HL7 v2, X12 and internal APIs. Run and maintain Own the existing AI codebase, prompts, tools and pipelines: document them, refactor them, and put them under version control with tests. Build and run an evaluation suite (golden sets, regression tests, LLM-as-judge with clinician spot checks) that gates every prompt, model or tool change. Monitor quality, latency, error rates, refusals, hallucination and drift in production; set alerts and on-call runbooks. Manage model selection, upgrades and deprecations across Claude tiers; keep prompts portable and rerun evals before every migration. Track and control spend: prompt caching, batch processing, model routing, token budgets, per-feature cost dashboards. Govern and comply Keep PHI safe: minimum-necessary data in prompts, de-identification where possible, no PHI in logs or traces, retention controls, and a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with every vendor that touches PHI. Support ONC certification: maintain documentation, source attributes and risk management for any AI that qualifies as a decision support intervention, and contribute to real-world testing and surveillance. Run AI risk assessments, bias and safety reviews, and incident response for AI errors, with clinical sign-off before launch. Keep an inventory of every AI use case, model, prompt version, data flow and owner. Collaborate Work with physicians, nurses, coders, billers and front-desk staff to find the highest-value use cases and to test outputs. Work with compliance, privacy and security officers on policies, audits and vendor reviews. Train staff on safe AI use, explain limits plainly, and collect feedback. Required technical skills Claude and LLM engineering (must have) Production experience with the Claude API: Messages API, system prompts, multi-turn state, streaming, structured and JSON outputs, tool use and parallel tool calls, extended thinking, vision and PDF input, citations, Files API, Batch API, and prompt caching. Model selection across the Claude family (fast/cheap versus most capable), with a measured cost, latency and quality tradeoff for each use case. Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK or an equivalent loop, including permissions, sandboxing, human-in-the-loop approval and failure recovery. Writing and securing MCP servers and clients; knowledge of Claude Code and Skills for engineering productivity. Access paths and their compliance differences: Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI; zero-data-retention and BAA terms. Advanced prompt engineering: role and context design, few-shot examples, XML-style structure, long-context handling, prompt versioning and A/B testing. Defending against prompt injection and data exfiltration, especially from documents, faxes, patient messages and web content that flow into prompts. Retrieval and data (must have) RAG design: chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, citation grounding, freshness and access control per user or role. Vector search (pgvector or equivalent) and full-text search; document parsing and OCR for scanned records and faxes. Strong SQL and relational modeling (PostgreSQL required; SQL Server a plus). Query tuning, indexing, migrations. ETL and data quality pipelines; handling of clinical and billing data with audit trails. Evaluation and quality (must have) Designing eval sets from real, de-identified cases; metrics for accuracy, groundedness, completeness, harmful-output rate and code or billing-field correctness. Automated regression testing in CI, LLM-as-judge with calibration against human reviewers, and online monitoring with sampled clinician review. Software engineering (must have) Strong Python and one of C#/.NET or TypeScript; our core applications are in the .NET and PostgreSQL ecosystem, so comfort reading and integrating with that code is expected. REST, WCF/SOAP and message-queue integration; async processing, retries, idempotency, rate-limit handling. Git, code review, automated tests, CI/CD, containers, infrastructure as code. Cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP) in a HIPAA-eligible configuration: VPC isolation, KMS encryption, secrets management, IAM least privilege. Observability and operations (must have) Structured tracing of prompts, tool calls and outputs with PHI redaction; dashboards for cost, latency, error and quality; alerting and runbooks. Security (must have) Encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, audit logging, secure SDLC, dependency and vulnerability management, threat modeling for LLM applications (OWASP LLM Top 10). Required healthcare and compliance knowledge The candidate must be able to apply these, not just name them. Priority: Must = required at hire, Learn = acceptable to learn in the first 90 days. Area What the candidate should know Priority HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Rules PHI and minimum necessary, BAAs, safeguards, audit controls, de-identification (Safe Harbor and Expert Determination), breach notification, AI-specific risks such as PHI leaking into prompts and logs Must ONC Health IT Certification Certification criteria our product holds, Cures Act information blocking rules, real-world testing, and the HTI-1 final rule requirements for decision support interventions (170.315(b)(11)), including source attributes, risk management and transparency for predictive models Must FHIR and interoperability FHIR R4, US Core, USCDI, SMART on FHIR, OAuth 2.0, the certified standardized API (170.315(g)(10)), C-CDA, bulk data; HL7 v2 messages (ADT, ORM, ORU, SIU) Must Billing and revenue cycle X12 837, 835, 270/271, 276/277, 278; claim lifecycle, denials and CARC/RARC codes, clearinghouse workflows, payer rules, patient statements and payment posting Must Medical coding ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, modifiers, E/M leveling, medical necessity, NCCI edits, risk adjustment basics Must Clinical workflow Visit documentation (SOAP), orders and results, e-prescribing, medication reconciliation, problem list, referrals, prior authorization Must Clinical terminologies SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, UCUM; mapping free text to codes Learn FDA and clinical decision support When software is a regulated device and the CDS exemption criteria; FDA guidance on AI-enabled software Learn Nondiscrimination and bias Section 1557 patient care decision support tools, bias testing across demographic groups Must State and payer AI rules State laws on AI disclosure in patient communication, telehealth and privacy; payer rules on AI in utilization review and prior authorization Learn Security frameworks NIST CSF, NIST AI RMF, HITRUST or SOC 2 awareness, 42 CFR Part 2 for substance use records Learn Patient safety Escalation design, clinician-in-the-loop, error reporting, and the difference between administrative and clinical AI risk Must Broader AI knowledge expected We use Claude, but the engineer must see the whole field so we pick the right tool and are never locked in by habit. Other LLM providers and open models: working knowledge of OpenAI, Gemini and open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen), and when self-hosting is justified for PHI, cost or latency reasons. Ability to run a fair head-to-head bake-off. Classical machine learning: supervised learning, gradient boosting, calibration, and validation for risk scores, no-show prediction, denial prediction and propensity models; scikit-learn, XGBoost or similar. NLP and information extraction: clinical named entity recognition, de-identification models, classification and entity resolution; when a small fine-tuned model beats a large LLM. Speech and ambient scribing: speech-to-text (Whisper-class and commercial medical ASR), diarization, medical vocabulary handling, and consent and recording-law considerations. Document AI: OCR, layout analysis, fax and scanned-form ingestion, insurance card and EOB extraction. Multimodal models: image and PDF understanding; clear limits on any diagnostic imaging use, which is out of scope without regulatory review. Fine-tuning and adaptation: when fine-tuning, distillation or retrieval is the right lever, and how to validate each. Responsible AI: hallucination and automation-bias mitigation, explainability suited to clinicians, fairness testing, model cards, drift monitoring, and incident reporting. Standards and frameworks: NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001 awareness, CHAI and Joint Commission guidance on responsible AI in health care. Awareness of the market: commercial ambient scribe, coding and revenue cycle AI vendors, so we can judge build versus buy. Experience, education and personal qualities Experience 4+ years of professional software engineering, including 2+ years building and operating LLM or ML systems in production. [Adjust for seniority] At least one shipped LLM application with real users, an eval suite and monitoring. 2+ years in health care, health IT or another regulated domain (finance, insurance), with direct handling of PHI or equivalent sensitive data. Hands-on integration with an EHR, practice management or billing system. Education Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, informatics or a related field, or equivalent experience. A master's degree or health informatics certificate is a plus. Nice to have Experience with an ONC-certified product or the certification process, or with a Waystar or similar clearinghouse integration. Clinical or coding credentials (CPC, CCS, RHIA, RN) or prior work alongside clinicians. HIPAA, security or AI governance certifications (CHPS, CISSP, Security+, AIGP). Experience migrating legacy .NET or SQL Server systems to PostgreSQL. Open-source or published work on LLM evaluation, safety or health AI. Personal qualities Clear communicator who can explain model limits to a physician and a biller in their own language. Careful and skeptical: treats every AI output as a claim to be verified, and says no to unsafe shortcuts. Pragmatic: prefers the simplest solution that works, and measures before and after. Comfortable with ownership, documentation and on-call, in a small team without a large platform group. Ethical and discreet with patient information. First 90 days and success measures Period Outcomes Days 1 to 30 Complete HIPAA and security training. Inventory every existing AI use case, prompt, tool, data flow and vendor agreement. Read the codebase and shadow clinicians and billers. Deliver a gap report covering evals, monitoring, PHI handling and cost. Days 31 to 60 Put existing prompts and tools under version control with tests. Stand up a baseline eval suite and production dashboard for the top two AI workflows. Fix the highest-risk PHI and security gaps. Days 61 to 90 Ship one measurable improvement or new feature through the full process (eval, clinical sign-off, staged rollout). Publish the AI governance checklist and incident runbook. Present a 12-month AI roadmap with build-versus-buy and cost estimates. Ongoing success measures Every production AI feature has an owner, an eval suite, monitoring and a documented risk review. Zero PHI incidents attributable to AI systems. Measured gains, such as minutes saved per visit note, clean-claim rate, denial rate, days in A/R and staff satisfaction, tracked against a pre-AI baseline. Cost per task stays within agreed budgets, and model upgrades ship without quality regressions. Clinician and staff trust, measured by periodic survey and sampled review. 2-5 Yrs Machine, Python, Full Stack, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning Algorithms, Aiml, Machine learning, Development

Use modern frameworks and agile practices to deliver scalable, high-performing solutions tailored to specific business needs. Must have skills : Embedded Product Verification & Validation Good to have skills: NA Minimum 3 year(s) of experience is required Educational Qualification: Bachelors degree in Computer Science or Software Engineering Computer or Electrical Engineering or Automotive Engineering or equivalent technical experience Summary: The Senior Analyst will create and maintain simulation test scenarios derived from real-world system logs and telemetry. The role requires strong diagnostic reasoning, an understanding of complex software architectures and state machines, and the ability to translate observed system behavior into precise, bounded simulation parameters. The Senior Analyst will develop reusable configurations and programmatic rulesets that work reliably across varied automated data pipelines, rather than relying on single-instance scenario creation. Roles & Responsibilities: Perform log-based test generation and maintenance, with a focus on diagnostic accuracy and reproducible simulation scenarios. Analyze system logs and real-world telemetry to identify relevant events, infer system states, isolate variables and investigate the causes of observed behavior. Define strict inclusion criteria for selecting log events and translate them into bounded simulation parameters. Understand how software modules, state machines, environmental physics and simulator configurations interact to produce the behavior under test. Define scenario logic using Boolean conditions, geometric constraints and time-based predicates within dynamic 3D environments. Develop reusable configurations, test parameters and programmatic rulesets that can be applied in bulk across highly variable automated data pipelines. Design boundary-value and edge-case tests, with clear metrics and tolerances that isolate the intended signal while allowing acceptable minor execution variances. Maintain scenarios and configurations as system behavior, source logs and simulation inputs change, checking that the intended test conditions remain valid. Review scenario definitions and diagnostic findings for clarity, consistency and traceability to the source telemetry. Professional & Technical Skills: Strong deductive reasoning and analytical judgment to reverse-engineer observed behavior and troubleshoot complex issues. Systems-level thinking, with the ability to move from individual scenarios to reusable rules that support large-scale automated execution. A structured and detail-oriented approach to defining inclusion criteria, documenting assumptions and checking diagnostic conclusions. Clear technical communication and the ability to explain scenario logic, system interactions and findings to a distributed team. Systems Architecture & Modular Thinking: Understand complex, interdependent software architectures and state machines, including the interaction of discrete modules, environmental physics and simulator configurations. Log Analysis & Diagnostic Troubleshooting: Parse system logs, interpret telemetry, isolate variables and translate real-world events into accurate, bounded simulation parameters. Parametric Design & Spatial Logic: Apply Boolean logic, geometric constraints and time-based predicates to dynamic 3D environments. Algorithmic Scalability: Design configurations and test parameters that remain reliable across variable automated data pipelines, using programmatic rulesets that can be applied in bulk. Robustness & Boundary Value Analysis: Identify edge cases, define suitable tolerances and design metrics that distinguish the intended signal from acceptable minor execution variances. Configuration & Visual Logic Tools: Experience with visual node-based logic, such as Unreal Engine Blueprints or Unity, or complex configuration languages such as JSON and XML is beneficial. Relevant Backgrounds: Experience in QA automation engineering, data analysis, Tier 3 technical support or systems integration may provide a suitable foundation when supported by the core competencies above. Additional Information: - The candidate should have minimum 7 years of experience in Test and Embedded Product Verification & Validation. - This position is based at our Bengaluru office. - A Bachelors degree in Computer Science or Software Engineering Computer or Electrical Engineering or Automotive Engineering (Systems and Controls), Applied Mathematics, Physics, or equivalent technical experience is required. Qualification Bachelors degree in Computer Science or Software Engineering Computer or Electrical Engineering or Automotive Engineering or equivalent technical experience 7-12 Yrs Physics, Architecture, Mathematics, Embedded systems, Application, Data, Automotive, Quality assurance

The role translates high-level behavioral requirements, hypothetical test intents and diagrams into clear, parameterized test scenarios. The Senior Analyst will independently handle assigned testing activities, analyze results, investigate defects and work with software and simulation engineering teams to resolve issues. The focus is on delivering diverse, robust scenarios that test the intended behavior while respecting physical and logical constraints, with clear documentation and handovers across US and India teams. Analyze high-level test intents, diagrams and behavioral requirements to define scenario specifications, parameters and acceptance criteria clarify gaps with the Test Lead and engineering teams. Design diverse scenario permutations using combinatorial testing to meet coverage goals while avoiding unnecessary duplication. Analyze interactions between software modules, state machines, environmental physics and simulator configurations to ensure scenarios test the intended system behavior. Develop and maintain reusable configuration rules and parameter sets for reliable bulk generation and execution across automated data pipelines. Apply scenario quality checks, boundary conditions, tolerances and metrics to distinguish genuine behavioral issues from acceptable execution variation. Execute scenarios, analyze results and investigate failures document reproducible defects and work with software and simulation engineering teams on retesting and closure. Update assigned scenarios as requirements, simulator configurations and testing methodologies evolve, and assess the impact on existing coverage. Estimate effort for assigned work, track progress and provide clear handovers across US and India teams escalate dependencies and delivery blockers to the Test Lead. Participate in peer reviews and share technical knowledge with colleagues working across simulation engineering, technical art, level design and procedural generation. Maintain accurate records of scenario coverage, execution results, defects and maintenance needs, and communicate findings and technical risks to the Test Lead and relevant engineers. Support evolving methods, including synthetic transformation of logged events and procedural agent injection into real-world telemetry Professional & Technical Skills: Work planning and ownership: Ability to estimate effort, prioritize assigned activities and deliver testing and maintenance work against agreed timelines. Technical independence: Ability to develop and troubleshoot scenarios independently, seek clarification when needed and contribute to peer reviews and knowledge sharing. Analytical thinking: Strong problem-solving skills to break down complex requirements, identify dependencies and make evidence-based decisions. Clear communication: Ability to explain test findings, defects, technical constraints and risks clearly to the Test Lead and engineering stakeholders. Global collaboration: Ability to work effectively with distributed teams, communicate dependencies and maintain clear cross-location handovers. Quality focus: A structured approach to scenario checks, documentation, traceability and reproducible issue reporting. Adaptability: Ability to work with different specialist skills and adjust testing approaches as methods and tools evolve Systems architecture and modular thinking: Strong understanding of interdependent software architectures, state machines and the interactions between software modules, environmental physics and simulator configurations. Parametric design and spatial logic: Ability to apply Boolean logic, geometric constraints and time-based conditions to dynamic 3D environments. Synthetic scenario design: Ability to translate abstract test intents and diagrams into realistic, varied scenarios that challenge behavioral requirements without violating physical or logical constraints. Combinatorial testing: Ability to design parameter combinations that provide broad, meaningful coverage without unnecessary overlap. Algorithmic scalability: Ability to define reusable, programmatic rulesets and configurations that remain reliable across variable inputs and high-volume automated pipelines. Robustness and boundary value analysis: Strong understanding of edge cases, tolerances and metrics that isolate the intended signal while allowing acceptable execution variation. Simulation configuration: Ability to review and troubleshoot scenario configurations, system states and simulator behavior. Tools and configuration languages: Experience with visual node-based tools such as Unreal Engine Blueprints or Unity, or configuration languages such as JSON and XML, is beneficial. Scenario lifecycle management: Ability to maintain reusable scenario libraries and assess the impact of changes to requirements, configurations and simulation environments. Evolving testing methods: Understanding of synthetic transformation of logged events and procedural agent injection into real-world telemetry is beneficial. jobs.title: Senior Director AI/ML Engineering
jobs.description: Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, data and resources they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits and career development opportunities. Come make an impact on the communities we serve as you help us advance health optimization on a global scale. Join us to start Caring. Connecting. Growing together. An SG31 Senior Director, AI/ML Engineering is a senior technology executive responsible for leading enterprise AI initiatives from strategy through execution and value realization. The role provides leadership for AI engineering organizations and serves as the accountable owner for AI platforms, intelligent automation capabilities, machine learning solutions, and emerging AI technologies that support business transformation. The position focuses on delivering measurable business outcomes through AI while ensuring scalability, reliability, security, and governance. The Senior Director is responsible for setting the technical and business direction for AI programs, establishing multi-year roadmaps, prioritizing investments, and aligning technology execution with organizational goals. They work closely with business leaders, product teams, operations partners, architecture groups, and executive leadership to identify opportunities where AI can improve efficiency, reduce cost, enhance customer experiences, and create new capabilities. Success is measured not only by technology delivery but also by adoption, operational impact, productivity gains, and financial value creation. As a people leader, the role oversees a team of engineering leaders, AI engineers, machine learning engineers, data scientists, and platform specialists distributed across onshore and offshore locations. Responsibilities include organizational design, talent strategy, workforce planning, hiring, performance management, leadership development, and succession planning. The Senior Director creates an environment of innovation, accountability, continuous learning, and engineering excellence while building a solid leadership bench capable of scaling enterprise AI capabilities. From a technology perspective, this leader owns the end-to-end lifecycle of AI solutions, including platform architecture, model deployment, intelligent agents, automation frameworks, cloud infrastructure, production operations, observability, and reliability engineering. The role ensures that AI capabilities are developed as reusable enterprise assets rather than isolated solutions, enabling faster adoption and greater return on investment across multiple business domains. The position carries significant accountability for Responsible AI, compliance, security, and risk management. The Senior Director ensures that all AI solutions comply with governance requirements, regulatory obligations, ethical AI principles, privacy standards, and operational controls. They establish processes for model monitoring, performance measurement, incident management, human oversight, and continuous improvement to maintain trust and reliability at enterprise scale. The role requires solid executive presence and the ability to influence senior leaders across the organization.
